title: Method and Instrumented Fixture for Femoral Fracture Testing in a Sideways Fall-on-the-Hip Position
protocol: Remove standard fixtures from the machine.
Move crosshead apart to accommodate the in-house fixture.
Place the aluminum block on the machine and securely fasten it using two bolts.
Place the main fixture structure on the aluminum block and attach it securely using 4 bolts.
Support the part of the fixture that does not rest on the aluminum block with a four-ton jack.
Mount the 6-channel load cell fixture on the main fixture and secure it using 6 screws.
Set the machine crosshead to absolute zero using crosshead lift control.
Attach first baseplate to the crosshead using 7 screws, with its curved edges facing the front of the testing machine.
Attach second baseplate using one pivoting screw.
Allow the second baseplate to swivel about the pivot screw relative to first baseplate.
Attach the assembly of the two slide bearings to the second baseplate using 4 screws (two screws can be accessed from one side of the first baseplate).
Rotate the second baseplate in such a way that the second set of screws can be accessed from the top of the first baseplates.
Set up the instrumented bottom fixture on a standard servo hydraulic testing machine.
Position high intensity lights on tripods with one on each side of the machine and secure them.
Set up tripods for high-speed cameras on either side of the testing machine.
Connect each camera to data acquisition units.
Configure camera settings; set frame rate to 6000 frames per second (fps).
Set resolution to 1,024 x 512 pixels.
Reduce resolution if necessary to accommodate camera internal memory.
Set shutter speed to 1 frame/sec (1/6,000 fps).
Set the camera option for recordings to begin before actuator movement; set delay to 100 ms for fast tests and 200 ms for slow tests.
Connect the synchronizing cable between the two cameras.
Select trigger mode in the software setting of the cameras.
Connect the DAQ unit to the testing machine, high-speed video camera, load cells, and linear potentiometer as shown in wiring schematic.
Check proper connection of trochanteric load cell by observing data signal traces in the view panel of the DAQ software.
Manually push on the head load cell to verify its proper connection and observe data signal traces.
Verify 6-channel load cell connection by observing data signal traces in the view panel of the DAQ software.
Check trigger signal connection to the DAQ device by observing data signal traces.
Ensure the DAQ, Signal Conditioner, and Pulse Generator are all powered ON.
Configure the DAQ software for all signals from the load cells and the linear potentiometer.
Select the "Step setup >> Configuration" tab in the DAQ software.
Set up the acquisition rate (Hz) for each signal input associated with each load cell.
On the "Triggering" tab, select the appropriate triggering option.
Trigger video equipment during trial runs to ensure video/DAQ system synchronicity.
Apply a nominal load of 200 lbs to 1600 lbs to the femoral head and trochanter load cells using a standard servo hydraulic machine.
Verify reasonable load cell measurements by comparing them with manufacturer calibration data sheets.
Apply static loads to the 6-channel load cell using a dead weight.
Check the functionality and verify performance of the 6-channel load cell by calculating percent differences between measured and theoretical force and moment values.
Ensure that all load cells have been calibrated by their manufacturers in advance.
Calibrate the linear potentiometer.
Secure the linear potentiometer fixture to the crosshead.
Place the linear potentiometer in the fixture.
Tighten screws to lock the potentiometer body.
Plug the connector into the DAQ unit.
Manually move the actuator on the load frame (25 mm).
Record displacements and corresponding voltage for at least three data points.
Plot displacement vs. voltage.
Fit a linear function to the data (R² > 0.95).
Input the slope of the linear equation (mm/V) as the calibration factor into the "Scaling parameter" box of the DAQ software.
Verify the overall testing machine setup by testing a surrogate fiberglass bone to fracture.
Thaw bones at room temperature for 24 hours.
Remove moisture, excess fat, and any remaining soft tissue using paper towels.
Place bone in the acrylic scanning fixture.
Prepare dental cement.
Measure 60 g of PMMA powder.
Mix with 30 g of liquid resin under fume hood until the powder has dissolved.
Use a disposable paper cup for this process.
Align the aluminum cup below the trochanter.
Pour PMMA cement to half the height of the cup.
Raise the fixture platform to fit the bone into the cup.
Wrap bones in saline-soaked towels.
Move bone to the test fixture with aluminum cup attached to trochanter.
Center the aluminum cup on the plate attached to the trochanteric load cell.
Adjust slide bearings so that the aluminum cup slightly touches the load cell.
Remove the pin from the fixture to allow for rotation of the fixture.
Center and lower the crosshead for contact with the femoral head.
Review setup, bone position, load cell signals, and cup position.
Ensure all equipment and load cells are connected properly and powered on.
Check software setup for proper signal response from each load cell.
Take pictures of the femur placed in the fixture from two sides.
Set the aperture to allow enough light onto the camera sensor.
Control the depth of field to check image quality by focusing on the femoral neck.
Verify lighting to minimize reflections in the video cameras.
Verify the data acquisition system one final time.
Click on the start icon from the control panel to initiate test sequence.
Take pictures of the fractured femur from two sides.
Manually retract actuator and remove femur from machine.
Remove bone from fixture.
Tape proximal broken end of bone to shaft.
Wrap bone in wet towels and plastic bags.
Freeze wrapped bone at -20 °C.
